chapter: Lee and Lester Young band remembered
title: Lee Young as leader; writing for the band; why Lester left Basie
summary: Lee Young led the band and was the sole abstainer; Rowles wrote charts, Lester kept his part in his pocket, and nobody knows why he left Basie.

story.theme_name: Lester Young: the man, the sound, the Basie years
story.community_name: Remembering Lester Young: Prez the man and his sound

blocks.x: Were Lee and Lester co-leaders of that band?
Lee would take care of business??

Yeah, and he played all the drums -- which was terrible. He had a reputation for being... Like, he would speed up the tempo so much that you just couldn't believe it, and you couldn't play with him. But then, yet, he was the leader.

And he was the only one in the band that didn't have any bad habits. Like, he didn't drink, he didn't smoke, every intermission he'd go kitty-corner across the street into the drugstore and have a milkshake or a dish of ice cream or something like that, and the rest of the guys would all be playin' tonk and drinkin' and carryin', you know, and sneakin' around the corner smokin' something, or something like that, you know. Not Lee. No. Lee would sit over here and just... Lee would sit over here... He had a little whistle signal [DEMONSTRATES]; you could hear it. That
As far as the musical policy was concerned, did Lee handle that, too, or was that Lester's...?

That was sort of everybody. Nobody really... I wrote a whole lot of stuff for that band. The funny part about it is that Lee insisted that we memorize the music, and nobody used it. So I wrote out a chorus on "Body And Soul," and Lester could never remember his part -- because he was in the middle; you know, he wasn't playing the lead. And he used to say, "Wait a minute, wait a minute," and he reached in his back pocket and he pulled this thing out, folded up, and he'd fold it over the edge of the piano, and he'd play it with his head hanging down, he'd play his part... Jesus, I used to laugh... Everybody laughed. But he wouldn't quit. He carried that part around with him all the time. If he lost that part, though, he was in trouble.
Did he ever talk about why he left Basie?

That's one of the big mysteries. Because Basie wouldn't talk about it, he wouldn't talk about it. And nobody seems to know whether he just got bored playing in a big band, whether he felt that he was ready to go out on his own or whether there was some problem.
